# From this, we see ADHD_diag is the first factor, then ADHD_notdiag. Hopefully defining the function in local scope overrides, but with R, you never know.

add_polr_row = function(curr_data, df, i, task_competency) {
  colname = colnames(curr_data)[i]
  print(paste("THIS IS THE TEST: ", colname))
  curr_data[[i]] = ordered(curr_data[[i]])
  
  # Make formula into string using paste
  # Simplest model
  formula = ""
  if (is.null(task_competency)) {
    formula = paste(colname, "~ group + yoe + pmh_avg + wfh_status")
  }
  else {
    formula = paste(colname, "~ group + yoe + pmh_avg + wfh_status +", task_competency)
  }
  
  print(formula)
  
  m = polr(formula, data = data, Hess = TRUE, na.action = na.omit)
  
  # Check prop odds assumption
  br = brant(m)
  omnibus = br[1, 3]
  
  # Check to see if the polr model is appropriate and keep that as data in the dataframe
  brant_pass = omnibus > .05
  
  # Extract z-values from the summary
  summary_polr = summary(m)
  z_values = summary_polr$coefficients[, "t value"]
  
  # Calculate p-values
  p_values = 2 * pnorm(-abs(z_values))
  if (is.null(task_competency)) {
    p_values = p_values[1:7]
  }
  else {
    p_values = p_values[1:8]
  }
  
  print(confint(m))
  new.row = data.frame()
  
  # Extract coefficients
  coefficients = coef(m)
  
  # Calculate odds ratios for each coefficient -- basically an effect size for how much sway each predictor has on the response variable. Increase by 1, or from reference value, increases the likelihood of increasing the response
  # variable by one level by [odds ratio] times
  odds_ratios = exp(coefficients)
  
  if (is.null(task_competency)) {
    new.row = data.frame(challenge = colname,
                         can_use = brant_pass,
                         adhdp = p_values[1],
                         audhdp = p_values[2],
                         ndp = p_values[3],
                         yoep = p_values[4],
                         pmhp = p_values[5],
                         hybridp = p_values[6],
                         wfhp = p_values[7])
  }
  
  else {
  new.row = data.frame(challenge = colname,
                         can_use = brant_pass,
                         adhdp = p_values[1],
                         audhdp = p_values[2],
                         ndp = p_values[3],
                         yoep = p_values[4],
                         pmhp = p_values[5],
                         hybridp = p_values[6],
                         wfhp = p_values[7],
                        compp = p_values[8])
  }
  odds_ratio_df = as.data.frame(t(odds_ratios))
  if (is.null(task_competency)) {
    colnames(odds_ratio_df) = c("coef_adhd", "coef_audhd", "coef_nd", "coef_yoe", "coef_pmh", "coef_hybrid", "coef_wfh")
  }
  else {
    colnames(odds_ratio_df) = c("coef_adhd", "coef_audhd", "coef_nd", "coef_yoe", "coef_pmh", "coef_hybrid", "coef_wfh", "coef_comp")
  }
  new.row = cbind(new.row, odds_ratio_df)
  df = rbind(df, new.row)
  return(df)
}

Challenge Modeling By Software Task

# Factors to put in polr formula: competency at task, group, yoe, pmh, wfh_status

challenges_df = data.frame(challenge = character(),
                           can_use = logical(),
                           adhdp = numeric(),
                           audhdp = numeric(),
                           ndp = numeric(),
                           yoep = numeric(),
                           pmhp = numeric(),
                           hybridp = numeric(),
                           wfhp = numeric(),
                           compp = numeric(),
                           coef_adhd = numeric(),
                           coef_audhd = numeric(),
                           coef_nd = numeric(),
                           coef_yoe = numeric(),
                           coef_pmh = numeric(),
                           coef_hybrid = numeric(),
                           coef_wfh = numeric(),
                           coef_comp = numeric())

comp_i = 116 # This is the index of best.tasks._1, or perceived competency at code review.

for (i in 53:59) {
  # Add task competency as a predictor to the formula by passing it into the function
  task_competency = colnames(data)[comp_i]
  challenges_df = add_polr_row(data, challenges_df, i, task_competency)
  comp_i = comp_i + 1
}

# Make a dataframe that's just the p values, then unlist and do BH correction and cat onto og dataframe

p_val_challenges

# Combine all p-values into a single vector

# Apply BH correction to the combined p-values
all_pvalues_corrected = p.adjust(all_pvalues, method = "BH")

# Reshape the corrected p-values back into the original dataframe

colnames(df_corrected) = c("adhdp_adjusted", "audhdp_adjusted", "ndp_adjusted", "yoep_adjusted", "pmhp_adjusted", "hybridp_adjusted", "wfhp_adjusted", "compp_adjusted")

# Make a dataframe that's just the p values, then unlist and do BH correction and cat onto og dataframe

p_val_challenges

# Combine all p-values into a single vector
all_pvalues = unlist(p_val_challenges)

# Apply BH correction to the combined p-values
all_pvalues_corrected = p.adjust(all_pvalues, method = "BH")

# Reshape the corrected p-values back into the original dataframe

colnames(df_corrected) = c("adhddiagp_adjusted", "adhdnondiagp_adjusted", "ndp_adjusted", "yoep_adjusted", "pmhp_adjusted", "hybridp_adjusted", "wfhp_adjusted")

Strength Modeling

# Factors that could reasonably affect strengths: yoe, group, pmh (self efficacy)
strengths_df = data.frame(strat.name = character(),
                           can_use = logical(),
                           adhdp = numeric(),
                           audhdp = numeric(),
                           ndp = numeric(),
                           yoep = numeric(),
                           pmhp = numeric(),
                           coef_adhd = numeric(),
                           coef_audhd = numeric(),
                           coef_nd = numeric(),
                           coef_yoe = numeric(),
                           coef_pmh = numeric())

for (i in 116:126) {
  colname = colnames(data)[i]
  print(paste("THIS IS THE TEST: ", colname))
  data[[i]] = ordered(data[[i]])
  levels(data[[i]])
  # Make formula into string using paste
  # Simplest model
  formula = paste(colname, "~ group + yoe + pmh_avg")
  m = polr(formula, data = data, Hess = TRUE, na.action = na.omit)
  
  # Extract coefficients
  coefficients = coef(m)
  
  # Calculate odds ratios for each coefficient -- basically an effect size for how much sway each predictor has on the response variable. Increase by 1, or from reference value, indicates the likelihood of increasing the response
  # variable by one level by [odds ratio] times (> 1 value means more likely to be higher, < 1 equals more likely to be lower on the scale)
  odds_ratios = exp(coefficients)
  odds_ratio_df = as.data.frame(t(odds_ratios))
  colnames(odds_ratio_df) = c("coef_adhd", "coef_audhd", "coef_nd", "coef_yoe", "coef_pmh")
  
  # Check prop odds assumption
  br = brant(m)
  summary(br)
  
  omnibus = br[1, 3]
  
  # Check to see if the polr model is appropriate and keep that as data in the dataframe
  brant_pass = omnibus > .05

  # Extract z-values from the summary
  summary_polr = summary(m)
  z_values = summary_polr$coefficients[, "t value"]

  # Calculate p-values
  p_values = 2 * pnorm(-abs(z_values))
  p_values = p_values[1:5]
  print(p_values)
  print(confint(m))
  new.row = data.frame(strat.name = colname,
                       can_use = brant_pass,
                       adhdp = p_values[1],
                       audhdp = p_values[2],
                       ndp = p_values[3],
                       yoep = p_values[4],
                       pmhp = p_values[5])
  new.row = cbind(new.row, odds_ratio_df)
  strengths_df = rbind(strengths_df, new.row)
}
